programme.title: The Real History of Pirates
programme.desc: Very few pirates hit it big or try to bury their treasure on a deserted island; exploring the business aspect of piracy, which is one of the few aspects of life pirates can control; piracy is a no-prey, no-pay system; the risk of no pay is very real.

programme.title: The Real History of Pirates
programme.desc: The complex truths of piracy and the pirate life are much different from the common tale surrounding them; the real goals of those pirates who attack and overthrow maritime powers; how the pirate motto, "a merry life and a short one," comes to be.

programme.title: The Real History of Pirates
programme.desc: Pirates often let their captives go as they know what can go wrong with too many unhappy captives on a ship; pondering whether this prisoner release also applies to non-European men; the deep and complex relationships between pirates and enslavers.

programme.title: The Real History of Pirates
programme.sub-title: The Sea Dogs of Elizabeth I
programme.desc: Privateers and pirates at the time of Queen Elizabeth I thrive by finding trade and protection; the individual histories of the most famous, ambitious and wealthiest of the Sea Dogs; these are John Hawkins, Sir Francis Drake and Sir Walter Ralegh.

programme.title: The Vikings
programme.desc: Hostile Christian sources demonize the Vikings; Muslim accounts render them exotic; revisionist historians belittle the Norse raids; archeological finds combined with a study of the Norse sagas enrich the understanding of Scandinavia's medieval past.

programme.title: The Vikings
programme.sub-title: Land and People of Medieval Scandinavia
programme.desc: Scandinavia's landscape shapes its culture; dense forestation leads to close-knit communities; woodworking and sailing are the key means of long-distance travel; harsh winters engender skill in cold-weather commute; the emergence of great halls.

programme.title: The Vikings
programme.sub-title: Scandinavian Society in the Bronze Age
programme.desc: The physical evidence paints a picture of the Bronze Age in Scandinavia; Viking ancestors trade Arctic goods, amber and slaves in exchange for foreign copper and tin; new wealth fosters larger villages; the beginnings of the Norse pantheon.
